# Ep 12 — Why nobody finishes their language app streak

## Beat 1 — cold open
Hi everyone, welcome back to the channel. Today we're going to talk about language apps, which a lot of you have asked about in the comments.

## Beat 2
Language apps have been around for a long time. There are many of them. Some are free and some are paid.

## Beat 3
Here's the stat: most users quit within the first month. The streak counter is designed to keep you, but it mostly makes you feel guilty.

## Beat 4
Let me tell you about my own experience. I started in January. Then February came. Then I traveled for work. Then I came back.

## Beat 5
The real reason: the app rewards showing up, not getting better. You can hold a 300-day streak and still not order coffee.

## Beat 6
So what works instead? Short real conversations, even awkward ones, beat 1000 tapped flashcards.

## Outro
If this hit home, tell me your longest streak below. See you next week.

# Small teams ship faster when they write less process

A survey of 120 product teams under 15 people found that teams with fewer than three mandatory rituals per week shipped features 30% faster on average.

The biggest drag was not meetings themselves but status reporting: engineers spent up to 4 hours a week writing updates nobody read.

Teams that replaced written status with a shared board and one 15-minute sync reported higher satisfaction and fewer missed deadlines.

The authors warn this does not scale past ~20 people, where lightweight process starts to cause coordination failures.

Their advice: add process only in response to a real failure, and remove one ritual every quarter.
